text:
GitHub issue statuses just gave your AI workflow a shared map.

On Nov. 23, issue statuses and repository boards entered public preview. Agents can read and set the same task states people use.

What changed: open or closed is no longer the whole picture.
What it does: track Todo, In progress, In review, and more directly on issues. Group a repository board by status.
Why it matters: a creator's image task and a developer's fix both need a visible handoff, not another buried chat.

Try this this week:
Create one issue for one image batch. Specify the subject, palette, output count, and a pass/fail check. In a repository saved view, switch to Board and group by status. Use the review stage to inspect the result against that brief.

On Tech Thursday, we connected an image model through MCP in Copilot CLI. It generated the batch. The host still wasn't satisfied with the look. That is the gap between execution and acceptance.

The signal: agents are moving into shared workflows. A status can tell you where work stands. It cannot tell you whether the work is good.

These boards don't create an approval gate by themselves. In our content engine, publishing still waits for a human-approved, merged PR.

Save this for your next AI workflow.

GitHub issue statuses can tell your agent where the work stands. Not whether it's good.
